page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running at 2.7 GHz on the arm64 ARMv9 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and a massive local storage capacity of 120,000 GB delivered via NVMe SSDs. Network connectivity is supported by a 300 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance across multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation using Clang. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with both cached small-block and uncached large-block read operations ranking in the top tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top 10%, reflecting the efficiency of the DDR5 memory subsystem and high-core-count architecture. However, single-core performance and text generation for small LLM models are more modest, with the latter falling into the bottom 10%.

Given its massive local NVMe SSD storage capacity and high memory density, this bare-metal instance offers high resource density for data-intensive deployments. It is highly suitable for large-scale databases, high-throughput static web serving, and memory-bound distributed computing tasks. The absence of a GPU makes it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, but its high multi-core throughput and massive storage footprint make it an efficient choice for large-scale data warehousing, ETL pipelines, and high-performance storage-heavy workloads.
